# help createsharesetting
createsharesetting - Create a sharesetting.

SYNTAX
    createsharesetting [-add <ipaddr_list>? <options for host access>] sharesetting_name

DESCRIPTION
    The createsharesetting command creates the share setting in the system.

AUTHORITY
    Super, Edit
    Any role granted the sharesetting_create right

OPTIONS
    -add
        Specifies the client IP address and access permissions for share access.
        Use , to separate the IP addresses.
        Use ? to seperate client access permissions after the IP addresses.

        Following IP address formats are supported:
            Use "*" to allow access to share by any client.
            Use 192.168.1.0/24 for multiple clients to have access to shares in a subnet.

        Following client access permissions are supported.
            ro
                Specifies that the fileshare will be exported to client as read-only.

            rw
                Specifies that the fileshare will be exported to client as read-write. If not specified, it will be
                exported to client as read-write. The default access permissions for fileshare is read-write.

            root_squash
                Map requests from UID/GID 0 to the anonymous UID/GID. Note that this does
                not apply to any other UIDs or GIDs that might be equally sensitive, such as
                user "bin" or group "staff".

            no_root_squash
                Turn off root squashing.

            all_squash
                Map all UIDs and GIDs to the anonymous user.

            Following options will be applied by default and cannot be changed: sync, wdelay,
            sec=sys, subtree_check, secure, hide.

            sync
                Reply to requests only after the changes have been committed to stable storage.

            wdelay
                The NFS server will normally delay committing a write request to disc slightly if it
                suspects that another related write request may be in progress or may arrive soon.
                This allows multiple write requests to be committed to disc with the one operation
                which can improve performance.

            sec=sys
                Restricts the export to clients using the security sys which is the default - no
                cryptographic security.

            subtree_check
                This allows server checks the accessed file to be in the appropriate filesystem and also
                that it is in the exported tree.

            secure
                Requires that requests originate on an Internet port less than IPPORT_RESERVED (1024).

            hide
                If a server exports two filesystems one of which is mounted on the other, then the client
                will have to mount both filesystems explicitly to get access to them. If it just mounts the
                parent, it will see an empty directory at the place where the other filesystem is mounted.

SPECIFIERS
    <sharesetting_name>
        Specifies a share setting name up to 255 characters in length.

NOTES
    A sharesetting needs to be created before creating a fileshare.

EXAMPLES
    The following examples create sharesetting setting_demo which provides access to clients
    with specified ip address, access permissions and options. 

       cli% createsharesetting -add 1.1.1.1,2.2.2.2?ro,no_root_squash 100.100.100.100?ro,no_root_squash setting_demo

    The following example creates share setting object which provides access to clients 
    with specified ip address, default access permissions and options will be applied
    since the previliges and options are not specified. 

       cli% createsharesetting -add 1.1.1.1,2.2.2.2 100.100.100.100/24 setting_demo

    The following example creates a sharesetting object setting_demo.

       cli% createsharesetting setting_demo

    The following example creates a sharesetting object setting_demo and allows
       access to share by any client.

       cli% createsharesetting -add * setting_demo
